references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, Jesus urges inviting precisely the poor, crippled, lame, and blind to a banquet – the same groups that the host now sends his servant out to bring in ([ref:Luk 14:13|Luke 14:13]).

In Matthew's parallel account of the king's wedding feast, the king becomes angry when the invited guests refuse to come and sends his servants out onto the roads to gather all they can find ([ref:Matt 22:7-10|Matthew 22:7-10]).
The context for the parable: a man prepared a great banquet and sent his servant to call those who had been invited, but they made excuses ([ref:Luk 14:16-17|Luke 14:16-17]).

Wisdom sends out her servant girls to invite the foolish and those lacking understanding to her banquet – a motif mirrored in the host's sending of his servant to the poor and weak ([ref:Ordsp 9:1-6|Proverbs 9:1-6]).

Jesus describes his own ministry by saying that the blind see, the lame walk, and the poor have the gospel preached to them – the same groups now being invited into the feast ([ref:Luk 7:22|Luke 7:22]).

Isaiah prophesies that the Messiah will proclaim good news to the poor and bind up those with a broken heart – a prophetic background for why it is the weak and outcasts who are invited in ([ref:Jes 61:1-2|Isaiah 61:1-2]).

When Saul was looking for his father's donkeys, he found that the poor and lowly were invited to a sacrificial meal – an Old Testament parallel to the humble being brought into a banquet ([ref:1 Sam 9:13|1 Samuel 9:13]).
The host then sends his servant even further out – to the roads and hedges – to compel people to come in, so that the house may be filled ([ref:Luk 14:23|Luke 14:23]).

Isaiah prophesies that in the time of salvation the eyes of the blind will be opened and the feet of the lame will leap – an eschatological motif reflected in the fact that precisely the blind and lame are invited into the feast ([ref:Jes 35:5-6|Isaiah 35:5-6]).
Paul and Barnabas turn away from those who reject the gospel to others who will receive it, a parallel to the originally invited guests being replaced by other guests ([ref:Apg 13:46|Acts 13:46]).
